Gene-Environment Interaction Power Analysis

Placental xQTL Study

Analytical Power Calculations for SNP × Exposure Interactions

2026-04-24

Overview

This document presents analytical power calculations for detecting gene-environment (G×E) interaction effects in placental expression quantitative trait loci (xQTL) analysis. We calculate statistical power to detect SNP × exposure interaction effects on isoform expression under the following study design:

  • Total sample size: N = 2,126 placentas
  • Exposures: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM, ~20% prevalence) and pre-pregnancy BMI
  • Genetic variants: Common variants (MAF ≥ 0.05) in cis-regulatory regions
  • Outcome: Placental isoform expression (variance-stabilized)
  • Significance threshold: α = 0.05 (FDR-controlled for candidate loci)

Statistical Framework

Regression Model

We test for G×E interactions using linear regression:

\[ Y_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_G \cdot G_{ij} + \beta_E \cdot E_{ij} + \beta_{GE} \cdot (G_{ij} \times E_{ij}) + \mathbf{Z}_{ij}^T \boldsymbol{\gamma} + \varepsilon_{ij} \]

where:

  • \(Y_{ij}\) = variance-stabilized expression of isoform \(i\) in sample \(j\)
  • \(G_{ij}\) = genotype dosage at SNP \(i\) in sample \(j\) (0, 1, or 2 minor alleles)
  • \(E_{ij}\) = exposure status in sample \(j\) (binary: GDM yes/no; or continuous: BMI)
  • \(\beta_{GE}\) = interaction effect (primary parameter of interest)
  • \(\mathbf{Z}_{ij}\) = covariate vector (cohort, sex, gestational age, ancestry PCs, latent factors)
  • \(\varepsilon_{ij} \sim N(0, \sigma^2_\varepsilon)\) = residual error

Hypothesis Test

We test the null hypothesis of no gene-environment interaction:

\[ H_0: \beta_{GE} = 0 \quad \text{vs.} \quad H_A: \beta_{GE} \neq 0 \]

using an F-test (equivalent to t-test for single parameter):

\[ F = \frac{SS_{GE} / df_1}{SS_{residual} / df_2} \]

where \(df_1 = 1\) (numerator df) and \(df_2 = N - p - 1\) (denominator df, with \(p\) = number of predictors).

Effect Size

The interaction effect size is quantified using Cohen’s \(f^2\):

\[ f^2 = \frac{R^2_{GE}}{1 - R^2_{full}} \]

where:

  • \(R^2_{GE}\) = incremental variance explained by the interaction term
  • \(R^2_{full}\) = total variance explained by the full model

The incremental variance explained by the interaction is:

\[ R^2_{GE} = \frac{\beta^2_{GE} \cdot \text{Var}(G \times E)}{\sigma^2_Y} \]

where:

  • \(\text{Var}(G \times E)\) = variance of the genotype-exposure product
  • \(\sigma^2_Y\) = total phenotypic variance (assumed = 1 after variance stabilization)

Variance Components

Genotype Variance (assuming Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium)

\[ \text{Var}(G) = 2 \cdot p \cdot (1-p) \]

where \(p\) = minor allele frequency (MAF).

Exposure Variance

For binary exposure (GDM): \[ \text{Var}(E) = \pi \cdot (1 - \pi) \] where \(\pi\) = prevalence (0.20 for GDM).

For continuous exposure (BMI): \[ \text{Var}(E) = \sigma^2_E \] where \(\sigma_E\) is the standard deviation of the exposure (standardized to 1 after normalization).

Interaction Term Variance

For independent \(G\) and \(E\) (assuming no gene-environment correlation):

\[ \text{Var}(G \times E) = \text{Var}(G) \cdot \text{Var}(E) \]

Non-Centrality Parameter

Under the alternative hypothesis (\(H_A: \beta_{GE} \neq 0\)), the F-statistic follows a non-central F-distribution with non-centrality parameter:

\[ \lambda = f^2 \cdot df_2 = \frac{R^2_{GE}}{1 - R^2_{full}} \cdot (N - p - 1) \]

Statistical Power

Power is the probability of rejecting \(H_0\) when \(H_A\) is true:

\[ \text{Power} = P(F > F_{\alpha, df_1, df_2} \mid \lambda) \]

\[ = 1 - F_{df_1, df_2, \lambda}(F_{\alpha, df_1, df_2}) \]

where:

  • \(F_{\alpha, df_1, df_2}\) = critical value from the central F-distribution at significance level \(\alpha\)
  • \(F_{df_1, df_2, \lambda}(\cdot)\) = CDF of the non-central F-distribution with non-centrality parameter \(\lambda\)

Implementation

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Set theme for all plots
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))

Power Calculation Function

#' Calculate analytical power for G×E interaction test
#'
#' @param n Sample size
#' @param exposure_prev Exposure prevalence (for binary) or SD (for continuous)
#' @param maf Minor allele frequency
#' @param main_effect Main genetic effect size (β_G in SD units)
#' @param int_effect Interaction effect size (β_GE in SD units)
#' @param r2_cov Variance explained by covariates (R² from covariate-only model)
#' @param alpha Significance level (Type I error rate)
#' @param exposure_type "binary" or "continuous"
#' @param n_cov Number of covariates in model
#'
#' @return Statistical power (0 to 1)
calculate_gxe_power <- function(n, 
                                 exposure_prev, 
                                 maf, 
                                 main_effect, 
                                 int_effect,
                                 r2_cov = 0.35,
                                 alpha = 0.05,
                                 exposure_type = "binary",
                                 n_cov = 10) {
  
  # 1. Genotype variance (HWE assumption)
  var_g <- 2 * maf * (1 - maf)
  
  # 2. Exposure variance
  if (exposure_type == "binary") {
    var_e <- exposure_prev * (1 - exposure_prev)
  } else {
    var_e <- exposure_prev^2  # for continuous, input is SD
  }
  
  # 3. Interaction term variance (assuming independence)
  var_gxe <- var_g * var_e
  
  # 4. Residual phenotypic variance after covariates
  # Total variance = 1 (after variance stabilization)
  # Residual variance = 1 - R²_covariates
  residual_var <- 1 - r2_cov
  
  # 5. Variance explained by interaction (partial R²)
  # R²_GE = β²_GE × Var(G×E) / σ²_residual
  r2_int <- (int_effect^2 * var_gxe) / residual_var
  
  # 6. Cohen's f² effect size
  # f² = R²_GE / (1 - R²_full)
  # R²_full = R²_cov + R²_main + R²_GE
  # For conservative estimate, assume main effects explain additional variance
  r2_main <- (main_effect^2 * var_g) / residual_var
  r2_full <- r2_cov + r2_main + r2_int
  
  # Ensure R² doesn't exceed 1
  if (r2_full >= 1) {
    r2_full <- 0.99
  }
  
  f2 <- r2_int / (1 - r2_full)
  
  # 7. Degrees of freedom
  # Model: Y ~ G + E + G×E + covariates + intercept
  # Number of predictors (p) = 3 (G, E, G×E) + n_cov + 1 (intercept)
  p <- 3 + n_cov + 1
  df_num <- 1  # testing single interaction term
  df_denom <- n - p
  
  if (df_denom <= 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  
  # 8. Non-centrality parameter
  lambda <- f2 * df_denom
  
  # 9. Critical F-value (central F-distribution)
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_denom)
  
  # 10. Power (non-central F-distribution)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df_num, df_denom, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

Study Parameters

# Overall cohort
total_n <- 2126
gdm_prevalence <- 0.20
gdm_cases <- round(total_n * gdm_prevalence)
gdm_controls <- total_n - gdm_cases

# Ancestry-specific sample sizes
ancestry_data <- tibble(
  ancestry = c("White", "Black", "Hispanic/Latino", "East Asian", "South Asian"),
  n = c(1425, 238, 67, 342, 54),
  gdm_prev = 0.20  # assume similar prevalence across ancestries
)

# Model parameters
r2_covariates <- 0.35  # apriori defined
n_covariates <- 10     # cohort, sex, GA, 5-7 PCs, 1-2 latent factors
typical_eqtl_effect <- 0.40  # typical cis-eQTL effect size (SD units)

# Print summary
cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
## Study Design Parameters:
cat("------------------------\n")
## ------------------------
cat(sprintf("Total sample size: %d\n", total_n))
## Total sample size: 2126
cat(sprintf("GDM cases: %d (%.1f%%)\n", gdm_cases, gdm_prevalence * 100))
## GDM cases: 425 (20.0%)
cat(sprintf("GDM controls: %d (%.1f%%)\n", gdm_controls, (1 - gdm_prevalence) * 100))
## GDM controls: 1701 (80.0%)
cat(sprintf("R² from covariates: %.2f\n", r2_covariates))
## R² from covariates: 0.35
cat(sprintf("Number of covariates: %d\n", n_covariates))
## Number of covariates: 10
cat(sprintf("Typical eQTL effect size: %.2f SD\n", typical_eqtl_effect))
## Typical eQTL effect size: 0.40 SD

Power Analysis Results

Panel A: Power by Minor Allele Frequency

We calculate power across a range of interaction effect sizes for different MAF bins.

maf_values <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50)
int_effect_range <- seq(0.05, 0.50, 0.01)

power_by_maf <- expand_grid(
  maf = maf_values,
  int_effect = int_effect_range
) %>%
  mutate(
    power = map2_dbl(
      maf, int_effect,
      ~calculate_gxe_power(
        n = total_n,
        exposure_prev = gdm_prevalence,
        maf = .x,
        main_effect = typical_eqtl_effect,
        int_effect = .y,
        r2_cov = r2_covariates,
        exposure_type = "binary",
        alpha = 0.05
      )
    ),
    maf_label = paste0("MAF = ", maf)
  )

panel_a <- ggplot(power_by_maf, aes(x = int_effect, y = power, color = maf_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.47, y = 0.82, label = "80% power", 
           size = 3, color = "gray40") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "plasma", end = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0.05, 0.50, 0.05)) +
  labs(
    x = expression(paste("Interaction effect size (", beta[GE], ", SD units)")),
    y = "Statistical power",
    color = "",
    title = "Power by minor allele frequency",
    subtitle = paste0("N = ", format(total_n, big.mark = ","), 
                     ", GDM prevalence = ", gdm_prevalence * 100, "%")
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.85, 0.35),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "gray80"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(panel_a)

Higher MAF increases power because the genotype variance \(\text{Var}(G) = 2p(1-p)\) is maximized at MAF = 0.50. At 80% power, the minimum detectable interaction effect is \(\beta_{GE} = 0.16\) (MAF = 0.20) and \(\beta_{GE} = 0.14\) (MAF = 0.30). For context, cis-eQTL main effects in GTEx are typically quantified using normalized effect sizes (NES), which represent the slope of linear regression on normalized expression data1,2. Published eQTL studies report main effect sizes commonly in the range of 0.3-0.5 SD per allele when expression is variance-stabilized3,4, and interaction effects are generally smaller than main effects. Our detectable interaction effects of \(\beta_{GE} = 0.14-0.16\) therefore represent approximately 35-40% of a typical main eQTL effect, which is consistent with the expectation that G×E interactions require larger sample sizes to detect than marginal genetic effects5.

Panel B: Power by Ancestry Group

We assess power within each ancestry group separately to identify groups with limited detection capability.

int_effects_test <- c(0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35)

power_by_ancestry <- expand_grid(
  ancestry_data,
  int_effect = int_effects_test,
  maf = 0.20
) %>%
  mutate(
    power = pmap_dbl(
      list(n, gdm_prev, maf, int_effect),
      ~calculate_gxe_power(
        n = ..1,
        exposure_prev = ..2,
        maf = ..3,
        main_effect = typical_eqtl_effect,
        int_effect = ..4,
        r2_cov = r2_covariates,
        exposure_type = "binary"
      )
    ),
    int_label = paste0("β[GE] == ", int_effect)
  )

panel_b <- ggplot(power_by_ancestry, 
                   aes(x = reorder(ancestry, -n), y = power, fill = int_label)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0.3, end = 0.8,
                       labels = scales::parse_format()) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) {
    # Get sample sizes for each ancestry group
    n_vals <- ancestry_data$n[match(x, ancestry_data$ancestry)]
    paste0(x, "\nn=", n_vals)
  }) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Ancestry group",
    y = "Statistical power",
    fill = "Interaction\neffect",
    title = "Power by ancestry group",
    subtitle = "MAF = 0.20, GDM prevalence = 20%"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

print(panel_b)

The White ancestry group (N=1,425, 67% of total) achieves >80% power for interaction effects \(\beta_{GE} \geq 0.20\), enabling robust discovery of moderate GxE effects. East Asian (N=342) and Black (N=238) groups have moderate power (~40-65%) for larger effects (\(\beta_{GE} = 0.25-0.35\)), supporting replication analyses. Hispanic/Latino (N=67) and South Asian (N=54) groups have limited power (<20%) for ancestry-specific discovery. This distribution supports a discovery strategy prioritizing the White ancestry stratum, with trans-ancestry meta-analysis across all groups maximizing power and enabling heterogeneity testing.

Panel C: Minimum Detectable Effect Size

We determine the minimum interaction effect detectable at 80% power as a function of sample size.

# Panel C: Minimum detectable effect size by sample size and MAF
sample_sizes <- seq(100, 2500, 50)
target_power <- 0.80
maf_values_c <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50)

min_detectable_by_maf <- expand_grid(
  n = sample_sizes,
  maf = maf_values_c
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Binary search for minimum detectable effect
    min_effect = map2_dbl(n, maf, function(n_val, maf_val) {
      test_effects <- seq(0.05, 0.80, 0.01)
      powers <- map_dbl(test_effects, ~calculate_gxe_power(
        n = n_val,
        exposure_prev = gdm_prevalence,
        maf = maf_val,
        main_effect = typical_eqtl_effect,
        int_effect = .x,
        r2_cov = r2_covariates,
        exposure_type = "binary"
      ))
      # Find smallest effect with power >= target
      idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
      if (is.na(idx)) return(NA_real_)
      test_effects[idx]
    }),
    maf_label = paste0("MAF = ", maf)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(min_effect))

# Find value at current sample size for MAF = 0.20
current_mde <- min_detectable_by_maf %>%
  filter(n == total_n, maf == 0.20) %>%
  pull(min_effect)

panel_c <- ggplot(min_detectable_by_maf, aes(x = n, y = min_effect, color = maf_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = total_n, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("label", x = 2000, y = 0.05, 
           label = paste0("N = ", format(total_n, big.mark = ",")), 
           hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "gray30",
           fill = "white", label.size = 0.25) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "plasma", end = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.70), breaks = seq(0, 0.70, 0.10)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 2500, 500), labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    x = "Sample size",
    y = expression(paste("Minimum detectable interaction effect (", beta[GE], ")")),
    color = NULL,
    title = "Minimum detectable interaction effect at 80% power",
    subtitle = "GDM prevalence = 20%, α = 0.05"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = c(0.85, 0.80),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "gray80")
  )

print(panel_c)

At the current sample size (N = 2,126), we achieve 80% power to detect interaction effects of \(\beta_{GE} = 0.16\) SD. This represents a moderate effect size, consistent with the expectation that interaction effects are typically smaller than main genetic effects. The nonlinear relationship between sample size and detectable effect demonstrates diminishing returns beyond N = 2,000 for interactions in this range. Effects substantially smaller than \(\beta_{GE} = 0.15\) would require impractically large sample sizes (N > 3,000) for adequate power.

Panel D: Binary vs Continuous Exposure

We compare power for binary GDM exposure vs. continuous BMI exposure modeling.

int_effect_range_d <- seq(0.05, 0.50, 0.01)

power_comparison <- tibble(
  int_effect = int_effect_range_d
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Binary GDM
    power_gdm = map_dbl(
      int_effect,
      ~calculate_gxe_power(
        n = total_n,
        exposure_prev = gdm_prevalence,
        maf = 0.20,
        main_effect = typical_eqtl_effect,
        int_effect = .x,
        r2_cov = r2_covariates,
        exposure_type = "binary"
      )
    ),
    # Continuous BMI (standardized SD = 1)
    power_bmi = map_dbl(
      int_effect,
      ~calculate_gxe_power(
        n = total_n,
        exposure_prev = 1,  # SD after standardization
        maf = 0.20,
        main_effect = typical_eqtl_effect,
        int_effect = .x,
        r2_cov = r2_covariates,
        exposure_type = "continuous"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("power_"),
    names_to = "exposure_type",
    values_to = "power",
    names_prefix = "power_"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    exposure_label = case_when(
      exposure_type == "gdm" ~ "Binary GDM (20% prevalence)",
      exposure_type == "bmi" ~ "Continuous BMI (standardized)"
    )
  )

panel_d <- ggplot(power_comparison, 
                   aes(x = int_effect, y = power, color = exposure_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Binary GDM (20% prevalence)" = "#E31A1C", 
               "Continuous BMI (standardized)" = "#1F78B4")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0.05, 0.50, 0.05)) +
  labs(
    x = expression(paste("Interaction effect size (", beta[GE], ", SD units)")),
    y = "Statistical power",
    color = "Exposure type",
    title = "Binary vs continuous exposure modeling",
    subtitle = paste0("N = ", format(total_n, big.mark = ","), ", MAF = 0.20")
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.75, 0.30),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "gray80"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(panel_d)

Continuous BMI modeling provides substantially higher statistical power than binary GDM across all effect sizes due to increased exposure variance (\(\text{Var}(E) = 1.0\) vs 0.16). At 80% power, continuous BMI requires only \(\beta_{GE} = 0.08\) compared to \(\beta_{GE} = 0.16\) for binary GDM—a two-fold difference in minimum detectable effect.

Summary Tables

Minimum Detectable Effects at 80% Power

summary_stats <- tibble(
  MAF = c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50)
) %>%
  mutate(
    `Binary GDM` = map_dbl(MAF, function(m) {
      effects <- seq(0.05, 0.80, 0.005)
      powers <- map_dbl(effects, ~calculate_gxe_power(
        n = total_n,
        exposure_prev = gdm_prevalence,
        maf = m,
        main_effect = typical_eqtl_effect,
        int_effect = .x,
        exposure_type = "binary"
      ))
      idx <- which(powers >= 0.80)[1]
      if (is.na(idx)) return(NA_real_)
      effects[idx]
    }),
    `Continuous BMI` = map_dbl(MAF, function(m) {
      effects <- seq(0.05, 0.80, 0.005)
      powers <- map_dbl(effects, ~calculate_gxe_power(
        n = total_n,
        exposure_prev = 1,
        maf = m,
        main_effect = typical_eqtl_effect,
        int_effect = .x,
        exposure_type = "continuous"
      ))
      idx <- which(powers >= 0.80)[1]
      if (is.na(idx)) return(NA_real_)
      effects[idx]
    })
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3)))

summary_stats %>%
  kable(
    caption = paste0("Minimum detectable interaction effect (β_GE) at 80% power, N = ", 
                    format(total_n, big.mark = ",")),
    col.names = c("MAF", "Binary GDM (β_GE)", "Continuous BMI (β_GE)"),
    align = 'c'
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )

Ancestry-Specific Power

ancestry_power_summary <- ancestry_data %>%
  mutate(
    `β = 0.15` = map2_dbl(
      n, gdm_prev,
      ~calculate_gxe_power(.x, .y, 0.20, typical_eqtl_effect, 0.15, exposure_type = "binary")
    ),
    `β = 0.20` = map2_dbl(
      n, gdm_prev,
      ~calculate_gxe_power(.x, .y, 0.20, typical_eqtl_effect, 0.20, exposure_type = "binary")
    ),
    `β = 0.25` = map2_dbl(
      n, gdm_prev,
      ~calculate_gxe_power(.x, .y, 0.20, typical_eqtl_effect, 0.25, exposure_type = "binary")
    ),
    `β = 0.30` = map2_dbl(
      n, gdm_prev,
      ~calculate_gxe_power(.x, .y, 0.20, typical_eqtl_effect, 0.30, exposure_type = "binary")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-gdm_prev) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("β"), ~scales::percent(.x, accuracy = 0.1)))

ancestry_power_summary %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Power by ancestry group for different interaction effect sizes (MAF = 0.20, binary GDM)",
    col.names = c("Ancestry", "N", "β_GE = 0.15", "β_GE = 0.20", "β_GE = 0.25", "β_GE = 0.30"),
    align = 'c'
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE
  ) %>%
  row_spec(which(ancestry_power_summary$n < 200), bold = TRUE, color = "darkred")

Mathematical Appendix

Derivation of Non-Centrality Parameter

Starting from the regression model:

\[ Y = \beta_0 + \beta_G G + \beta_E E + \beta_{GE}(G \times E) + \mathbf{Z}^T\boldsymbol{\gamma} + \varepsilon \]

The F-statistic for testing \(H_0: \beta_{GE} = 0\) is:

\[ F = \frac{(RSS_0 - RSS_1)/1}{RSS_1/(N-p)} \]

where \(RSS_0\) is residual sum of squares under \(H_0\) and \(RSS_1\) under \(H_A\).

Under \(H_A\), this F-statistic follows a non-central F-distribution:

\[ F \sim F_{1, N-p}(\lambda) \]

with non-centrality parameter:

\[ \lambda = \frac{N \cdot \beta^2_{GE} \cdot \text{Var}(G \times E)}{\sigma^2_\varepsilon} \]

Since \(\text{Var}(Y) = 1\) (after variance stabilization) and \(\sigma^2_\varepsilon = 1 - R^2_{full}\):

\[ \lambda = \frac{N \cdot \beta^2_{GE} \cdot \text{Var}(G \times E)}{1 - R^2_{full}} \]

This can be rewritten as:

\[ \lambda = \frac{R^2_{GE}}{1 - R^2_{full}} \cdot (N - p) = f^2 \cdot (N - p) \]

where \(f^2\) is Cohen’s effect size for the interaction term.

Assumptions and Limitations

  1. Normality: Expression data assumed approximately normal after variance-stabilizing transformation (DESeq2)
  2. Independence: SNP and exposure assumed independent (no gene-environment correlation). Violated if genetic variants influence exposure status.
  3. Linearity: Interaction modeled as linear \(\beta_{GE} \cdot (G \times E)\). Non-linear interactions require different modeling.
  4. Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium: Genotype variance assumes HWE. Deviations reduce power.
  5. Homoscedasticity: Constant variance across genotype-exposure groups. Violations can be addressed with robust standard errors.
  6. No measurement error: Genotypes and exposures measured without error. GDM misclassification would reduce power.

These assumptions are reasonable for QTL mapping in well-phenotyped cohorts with high-quality genotyping.

References:

  1. GTEx Consortium. The GTEx Consortium atlas of genetic regulatory effects across human tissues. Science 369, 1318–1330 (2020).

  2. Mohammadi P, Castel SE, Brown AA, Lappalainen T. Quantifying the regulatory effect size of cis-acting genetic variation using allelic fold change. Genome Res 27, 1872–1884 (2017).

  3. GTEx Portal FAQ. “Normalized effect size (NES), previously known as the effect size on the portal, is defined as the slope of the linear regression.” Available at: https://sites.google.com/broadinstitute.org/gtex-faqs/home

  4. Mohammadi P, Castel SE, Cummings BB, Einson J, Sousa C, Hoffman P, et al. Genetic regulatory variation in populations informs transcriptome analysis in rare disease. Science 366, 351–356 (2019).

  5. Zablocki RW, Schork AJ, Levine RA, Andreassen OA, Dale AM, Thompson WK. Covariate-modulated local false discovery rate for genome-wide association studies. Bioinformatics 30, 2098–2104 (2014).
